html:
A French military column sent in 1899 to conquer the lands between the Niger and Lake Chad, led by captains Paul Voulet and Julien Chanoine, which burned villages and killed thousands of people across what is now southern Niger.

At Birni-N'Konni it massacred hundreds of inhabitants. When Paris sent Colonel Klobb to take command, Voulet had him shot, and soon after Voulet and Chanoine were killed by their own African soldiers. The column went on under other officers and reached Zinder. The story caused a scandal in France but no one was tried. It is remembered in Niger as the founding violence of French rule. See also the Scramble for Africa and Damagaram.
